text:
maria: Heads up — KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~94% to ~18% across gpu-pool-7 around 17:26 UTC, median p95 latency for chat-small jumped from 85ms -> 420ms. Not a full outage but lots of tail.

sre-bot: alert: kv_cache_hitrate_drop gpu-pool-7 severity=page

nate: omg, saw the alert. Any recent deploys or config changes to batching / cache?

aj: We shipped a batching heuristic tweak ~17:10 that increases max batching window from 12ms -> 30ms when qps > 40 to improve throughput. Also a minor autoscaler change for burst pools earlier today.

maria: sounds likely. Can someone pull the runtime profiler and cache stats for the pool?

ying: grabbing stats now. kv.{hits,misses,evictions} for the pool (1m windows):
```
17:00 hits=147890 misses=10234 evictions=98
17:20 hits=120345 misses=58421 evictions=4123
17:26 hits=21012  misses=90012 evictions=18902
```
This looks like an eviction wave starting ~17:20.

nate: eviction count spiked massively — memory pressure perhaps. Which tenants saw the largest live-kv size?

ying: tenant-summaries: one tenant (edge-qa) increased concurrent long-context requests at 17:12 — average seq_len x users jumped from 128 -> 1024 for a minute. That increased KV footprint per request.

aj: ah — batching window increase + a tenant sending long sequences will coalesce more tokens per batch and inflate total KV usage per device. The scheduler kept adding batches, memory hit threshold -> kernel selector started choosing fallback GEMM kernel that uses more temporary buffers. That can double peak mem.

maria: do we have profiler evidence for kernel selection flip?

ying: yes — runtime logs show: 
```
[17:18:03] kernel_selector: chosen=optimal_matmul cap=60mb
[17:20:14] kernel_selector: chosen=fallback_gemm cap=128mb reason=memory_pressure
[17:20:15] runtime: KV cache eviction triggered, freed=1.8GB
[17:20:25] kernel_selector: chosen=fallback_gemm cap=128mb
```

nate: fallback_gemm is slower and allocs temp buffers. So memory increases -> eviction -> cold misses -> worse latency = domino effect. Classic amplification.

aj: also saw batching logs:
```
[17:16:50] batch_coordinator: window=30ms qps=52 batch_size=14
[17:20:10] batch_coordinator: window=30ms qps=110 batch_size=48
```
That batch_size jump explains KV per-device surge.

maria: OK action plan? Rollback batching heuristic and throttle long-context tenant?

aj: propose two immediate mitigations: 1) rollback the max-window change (hotfix) 2) temporarily pin kernel_selector to prefer memory-efficient kernels (even if slower) to avoid huge temp buffers 3) apply per-tenant request-rate cap for edge-qa while we investigate.

deploy-bot: deploy start: revert-batching-heuristic -> canary on gpu-pool-7 (initiated by aj)

ying: started applying per-tenant throttle for edge-qa (60rps -> 12rps) to stop new long-seq storms.

maria: rolling rollback now, keeping an eye on hit-rate.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed on 3/3 nodes in gpu-pool-7

ying: quick post-rollback stats (1m window after canary):
```
17:28 hits=68012 misses=19834 evictions=412
```
Hit-rate back up to ~77% (from 18%). Latency p95 trending down to ~140ms.

nate: good. We should add a guard in batching coordinator: if per-device KV footprint > X then reduce batch size, irrespective of qps. Otherwise large sequences will cause global harm.

aj: Agreed. Also need a kernel-selection telemetry alert: if selector flips to fallback_gemm on > 20% of devices within 1m, fire an anomaly.

maria: can we get a short postmortem doc? I can draft — include timeline, root cause (batching window + tenant long seq -> kernel selection flip -> memory pressure -> eviction wave), mitigation, and follow-ups: batching guard, kernel-selector alert, per-tenant burst limits, and an e2e test that simulates concurrent long-seq flows.

ying: I'll capture the logs and profiler traces and dump a small perf trace snippet into the PM doc.

nate: one more note — check the autoscaler bump that let more batches run concurrently. It might have tightened thresholds that, combined with batching change, compounded the effect.

maria: adding that to follow-ups. Nice quick rollback everyone, thanks. :tada:

deploy-bot: action: rollback completed to config v=2026.03.17-rc3 (by aj)

ying: final stats 10m after rollback:
```
17:36 hits=118334 misses=10298 evictions=120
```
Hit-rate ~92%, p95 back near baseline. Leaving this thread open for the PM doc draft and postmortem attachments.

maria: I'll write and ping eng-oncall + eng-runtime with the postmortem draft in ~1 hour.

aj: I'll open a PR for batching guard and kernel-selector alerting.

nate: noted — will look into autoscaler thresholds too.

sre-bot: incident resolved: kv_cache_hitrate_drop gpu-pool-7 -> resolved (mitigation: rollback + tenant throttle)
